description: Sourced material/component limits and relations for abep_sim/thermal_life.py (THL lane). Every record is either 'sourced' (value transcribed from a document that was actually opened on the accessed_on date, with locator and evidence attributes per docs/EVIDENCE.md) or 'TBD' (no value; 'requires' says what is needed). thermal_life.py refuses (ValueError) to use a TBD record or a TBD value. Values are transcribed, never computed from repository data; the only transformations are the unit conversions stated in each record's transformation_chain. Nothing here is a Vyovrinda hardware measurement (evidence level 1-2 absent throughout).

vocabulary.evidence_level: 1-7 exactly as defined in docs/EVIDENCE.md (strength and proximity of the SOURCE for this application; never what was done to the number)

status.sourced: value(s) transcribed from the cited, accessed document
status.TBD: no usable value; 'requires' names what is needed; the module refuses to use it

vocabulary.value_null: a value of null inside a sourced record carries a 'TBD' string: that single quantity is not given by the source and must not be filled

copper_iacs_linear.locator: p. 3 (sec. 1.a International Annealed Copper Standard values; sec. 1.b a20 = 0.003 93 for 100 % conductivity annealed wire); p. 4 (IEC 0.00393 at 20 C for the resistance between points fixed on a freely expanding wire, based on Dellinger's NBS measurements 10-100 C; tables assume 'linear up to 200 C, and probably in the interval -100 to +300 C')
copper_iacs_linear.nature: international standard values (IACS, adopted by the IEC in 1913) resting on NBS measurements

rho_20C.as_published: 1.7241 microhm-cm at 20 C (also 0.017 241 ohm-mm2/meter at 20 C)

T_min_C.as_published: not a published bound: our domain choice (see transformation_chain)

T_max_C.as_published: the resistance-temperature curve for copper is linear up to 200 C

copper_iacs_linear.transformation_chain: measurement (Dellinger, 10-100 C) -> IACS/IEC standard values -> NBS HB100 text -> transcribed; microhm-cm -> ohm m (x 1e-8). Model R(T) = R20 [1 + a20 (T - 20 C)] as stated on p. 3. Domain: upper bound 200 C is the source's confident statement; the 'probably -100 to +300 C' extension is NOT used; lower bound 0 C is our choice (Roeser data straight from 0 C, p. 4).
copper_iacs_linear.uncertainty: for copper above 94 % conductivity the measured a20 agreed with the conductivity-derived value within 0.000 01 (about 0.3 %) (p. 3); a20 scales with percent conductivity (a20 = 0.003 93 x conductivity fraction, p. 3), so wire below 100 % IACS has a smaller a20
copper_iacs_linear.applicability_domain: annealed copper conductor (magnet wire), 0-200 C, resistance of a freely expanding wire
copper_iacs_linear.validation_status: standard reference value; not measured on Vyovrinda coil hardware

copper_roeser_ratio.locator: p. 4 (W. F. Roeser, unpublished NBS data for high-purity copper heated in vacuum; Rt/R0 table)
copper_roeser_ratio.nature: unpublished measurement reported by NBS (original not inspectable)
copper_roeser_ratio.transformation_chain: measurement -> NBS HB100 table -> transcribed -> our piecewise-linear interpolation in T, used only as a ratio R(T)/R(Tref). The source states the curve is a straight line from 0 to 300 C with slight upward curvature above; for a convex curve the chord between tabulated points lies above the curve, so the interpolation overestimates R (conservative for I^2 R heating).
copper_roeser_ratio.uncertainty: no uncertainty stated; high-purity copper has a larger relative resistance rise than lower-conductivity copper (a20 proportional to conductivity, p. 3), so using these ratios for ~100 % IACS wire overestimates the rise (conservative for heating; inferred from the p. 3 rule)
copper_roeser_ratio.validation_status: not validated on Vyovrinda coil hardware

hot_spot_allowance_K.as_published: note 1/a: maximum operating temperature equals ambient temperature plus temperature rise plus 10 C allowance for hot spots

life_basis_at_rating_h.as_published: note 1/b: insulation classes of MIL-style inductive parts generally have maximum operating temperature ratings based on a life expectancy of 10,000 hours

life_basis_at_derated_h.as_published: note 1/b: the derated operating temperatures are selected to extend the life expectancy to 50,000 hours at rated voltage

custom_derating_factor.as_published: note 1/c: custom made inductive devices shall be evaluated on a materials basis to determine the maximum operating temperature; devices with temperature ratings different from the military insulation classes shall be derated to 0.75 times maximum operating temperature

eee_inst_002_magnetics.transformation_chain: document text -> transcribed. Our interpretation (verify): the 0.75 factor is applied to the maximum operating temperature in C (Table 4 is in C); the 50,000 h life basis of note 1/b is stated for the Table 4 derated temperatures and is only inferred to carry over to the note 1/c factor
eee_inst_002_magnetics.uncertainty: engineering rule, no uncertainty stated; life bases are 'generally' / 'selected to' statements, not test results
eee_inst_002_magnetics.applicability_domain: EEE inductive parts (MIL-PRF-27, MIL-PRF-39010, MIL-PRF-15305, MIL-T-55631, custom magnetics) on GSFC projects; applying it to a Hall-thruster electromagnet is an analogy and an owner decision

lab6_richardson_goebel_table6_1.locator: Table 6-1 (p. 252); Eqs. (6.3-1)-(6.3-3) (p. 251): J = A T^2 exp(-e phi/kT), phi = phi0 + alpha T, J = D T^2 exp(-e phi0/kT)
lab6_richardson_goebel_table6_1.nature: Richardson-Dushman fit parameters to measured emission, compiled in a textbook from Lafferty 1951 [13], Jacobson & Storms 1978 [14], Storms & Mueller 1979 [15] and Kohl [8] (originals not inspected)
lab6_richardson_goebel_table6_1.transformation_chain: measured emission -> original fits -> Goebel & Katz Table 6-1 -> transcribed; A/cm2K2 -> A/m2K2 (x 1e4)
lab6_richardson_goebel_table6_1.uncertainty: the four sets are not reconciled by the source; thermal_life.py carries all four as an envelope (no set is selected or tuned). Cross-check: for the Kohl set D = A exp(-e alpha/k) = 28.8 A/cm2K2, consistent with Lafferty's D = 29
lab6_richardson_goebel_table6_1.applicability_domain: thermionic emission of LaB6 without surface field (the Schottky term, Eq. 6.3-4, is neglected: a required current density is then reached at a higher, i.e. conservative-for-evaporation, temperature)
lab6_richardson_goebel_table6_1.validation_status: literature; not validated on the Vyovrinda cathode

lab6_poisoning_goebel.locator: sec. 6.8.5 'Cathode Poisoning', p. 306 (diode tests, Fig. 6-49 from Goebel, Watkins & Jameson, JPP 23(3) 2007 [18])

T_no_degradation_min_C.as_published: LaB6 at 1570 C ... can withstand oxygen partial pressures up to 10^-4 torr without degradation in the electron emission

lab6_poisoning_goebel.transformation_chain: diode-test measurement -> Fig. 6-49 -> textbook sentence -> transcribed (only the stated no-degradation point is used; the figure itself is not digitized)
lab6_poisoning_goebel.uncertainty: single stated point; also stated: oxygen partial pressures 'in the 10^-5 torr range' are required to degrade LaB6 emission below 1440 C, and in 10^-3 torr O2 background the authors raised the temperature to just over 1600 C to avoid poisoning (p. 306) - context, not used as limits
lab6_poisoning_goebel.applicability_domain: molecular O2 partial pressure at the emitter; water and air poison at higher pressures; atomic-oxygen or O+ exposure (ABEP air path) is NOT covered
lab6_poisoning_goebel.validation_status: literature; not validated on the Vyovrinda cathode

lab6_usable_fraction_goebel.nature: assumption used in the source's evaporation-limited life estimate

usable_fraction.as_published: Assuming that 90% of the insert can be evaporated

lab6_usable_fraction_goebel.uncertainty: the source notes the estimate ignores temperature variations along the insert, surface removal and impurity build-up (life-reducing) and redeposition (life-extending); estimates are 'mostly valid relative to each other' (p. 303)

lab6_evaporation_rate.requires: a sourced LaB6 evaporation (mass-loss) rate versus emitter temperature, as a table (T_K, kg m^-2 s^-1) with provenance. Candidates: Goebel & Katz 2008 Fig. 6-8 (rate vs emission current density, from Leung, Pincosy & Ehlers, Rev. Sci. Instrum. 55, 1984 [24]) - graphical, needs digitization plus the A/phi set used to map J to T; Storms & Mueller, J. Chem. Phys. (LaB system vaporization) [23] - not accessed. No value is invented here. When sourced, the record must carry values T_K (list, K, increasing) and rate_kg_m2s (list, kg m^-2 s^-1, > 0), which thermal_life.lab6_evaporation_rate interpolates log-linearly inside the table only.

cathode_assembly_temperature_limit.requires: the limiting temperature of the cathode assembly node (heater insulation, orifice plate, keeper, LaB6 support/boron-diffusion barrier) from the cathode dossier, with source. When sourced, the record must carry the value T_max_C (degC)

rf_source_structure_limit.requires: the limiting temperature of the RF source structure node (antenna conductor and its insulation, dielectric tube/window, matching network) from the RF-source design, with a sourced material limit. When sourced, the record must carry the value T_max_C (degC)

ecr_source_structure_limit.requires: the limiting temperature of the ECR source structure node (waveguide/coupler, dielectric window, chamber) from the ECR-source design, with a sourced material limit. When sourced, the record must carry the value T_max_C (degC)

radiative_rejection.form: Q = eps sigma A F (T^4 - T_sink^4)

wall_ion_heat.locator: fields wall_ion_flux_m2s, wall_ion_energy_eV; bridge_lib.jl wall_ion_metrics returns (time-average of the cell-averaged Bohm flux, flux-weighted energy)
wall_ion_heat.form: Q_i = e Gamma_i eps_i A_wall (exact integral of the ion energy flux over z <= L when the grid is uniform)

wall_electron_heat.locator: Eq. (7.3-28) p. 348 (I_iw = I_ew (1 - gamma)); Eqs. (7.3-43), (7.3-45) p. 354 (electrons deposit 2 T_e each; secondary-electron cooling neglected); p. 358 (I_ew = electron wall power / 2 T_e)
wall_electron_heat.form: Q_e = e Gamma_i 2 T_e,w / (1 - gamma) A_wall

richardson_dushman.form: J = P T^2 exp(-e (phi0 + alpha T) / k T)

evaporation_limited_life.form: life = f_usable m_insert / (G_evap(T) A_emit), T = temperature required to emit the discharge current in the thermally limited regime

reversible_temperature_coefficient.locator: slides 11-13 (definition; Br(T) = Br20 [1 + RTC (T - 20)/100]; Hci(T) likewise; approximate away from the RTC calibration temperature; Br almost linear up to about 150 C); VAC brochure p. 34 (TK definitions)

irreversible_loss_criterion.locator: p. 34 'Influence of temperature' (the working point must remain within the linear section of the demagnetization curve over the entire temperature range to avoid irreversible changes); p. 16 (knee field H_K,90 and H_D5 per IEC 60404-8-1); MMPA 0100-00 p. 27 (irreversible losses definition)
irreversible_loss_criterion.form: |H_demag,max| < H_knee(T_magnet), with H_knee(T) from the grade's demagnetization curve at >= T_magnet
